newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't sees record privatization receipts.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't sees record privatization receipts.

text.p: The Brazilian government expects privatization receipts to total a record $4.5 billion in 1996, presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral said.
Amaral said up to end-October, 10 state firms had been sold or their services put out to concession, raising $3.7 billion in privatization proceeds.
"By the end of the year, receipts will be $4.5 billion, far superior to the previous record in 1993 of $2.7 billion," Amaral told reporters after a special cabinet meeting on Saturday.
Amaral said that in the cabinet meeting, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir had defended the privatization of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD).
Kandir told fellow ministers that CVRD was paying a "dividend" to the government of some 80 million reais per year.
"It's a very low return, only about 2.0 percent on the assets. This is much lower than we would get if we put the money into a savings account," Amaral quoted Kandir as saying.

The sell-off, slated to start in February with the block sale of 40-45 percent of voting shares, was expected to raise some 5.0 billion reais, which if used to retire debt, would save Brasilia 500 million reais a year in interest payments.

"Suppose you put all this money (500 million reais) into a fund to be used for infrastructure investment the federal government or the states need, the country's returns from CVRD would be much greater than they are today," Amaral said.

Quoting Kandir, Amaral said CVRD's other main purpose, which has been traditionally to serve as a catalyst for productive development in the country, was no longer so important now that Brazil had a significant industrial base.
The CVRD sale has faced mounting opposition in recent weeks, with former presidents Jose Sarney and Itamar Franco joining ranks to form a united front against the privatization.

States, which had originally been promised a slice of the pie, are claiming some of the proceeds for themselves and the government recently floated the idea of an infrastructure investment fund to meet their demands.
